swap_test.why_this_pair: The swap test runs the SAME brief against both snapshots, so both must be able to receive it — which disqualifies pairs where one side cannot (a marketing brief is meaningless for a personal training program). These two maximize range because the CORRECT answers share almost no structure: training blocks across hardware/software/pressure layers versus product and GTM workstreams. A plan that reads plausibly for both is, by construction, a template.
swap_test.runner_up: The Cadre — DJ Internal × Beyond Exit Planning. Set aside because two marketing engagements may legitimately share structure, compressing specificity_delta. Worth revisiting if marketing briefs need a dedicated pair; Beyond Exit Planning's compliance constraint (no promissory or investment-guarantee language) makes a template plan not merely generic but legally wrong.

artifact_shape_rule.rule: A plan is steps + effort estimates + stated knowns/unknowns, NOT a week-by-week schedule. Calendar framing ("Week 1 — ...", "Week 2 — ...") is a rubric violation even when the content is good: DJ rejected BOTH sample plans in the interview for exactly this framing, including the deliberately-strong Plan B.
artifact_shape_rule.dj_verbatim_c1: You can do time estimates of how certain things would be, but don't say, "Block week one, we would do this." I think it should lay out a general strategy for how we're gonna do stuff, and then it says the steps of the plan. I think in terms of steps rather than schedule, like, "These are the steps. These are the knowns and unknowns."
artifact_shape_rule.dj_verbatim_c2: Plan B is fine. I just wouldn't frame it in terms of week 1, week 2, week 3, week 4. I would frame it in terms of a sequence of steps and measure or guess the workload required for each part.
artifact_shape_rule.scoring_consequence: Checkable at L0 by code: flag week-block scaffolding as a violation; require per-step effort estimates and an explicit knowns/unknowns section. Also renames what ob-04 asks for — the brief may still scope four weeks of work, but the artifact must be step-sequenced, not calendar-blocked.

quality_bar_is_feasibility_not_specifici.rule: C5 redefines "it gets this project": the tell is SELF-ASSESSED FEASIBILITY — does the plan know whether there is enough context to achieve it, does it stress-test itself, does it weigh how hard it is, does it ask for what it needs — NOT specificity. Sprinkling real project nouns onto a skeleton (what grounding ratio and the swap test detect) is a supporting signal, not the bar.
quality_bar_is_feasibility_not_specifici.dj_verbatim_c5: It should know if we have enough context to achieve this plan. It should sort of stress test the plan. It would basically try to determine if this plan is doable. It would try to weigh how hard this plan is and how easy this plan is. It should ask for more context in order to make sure that the plan will actually get done and that the plan is feasible and followable.
quality_bar_is_feasibility_not_specifici.scoring_consequence: The L1 grounding ratio and L2 swap test measure specificity and stay useful as anti-template detectors, but they can no longer be the headline metric. The instrument needs a feasibility-self-assessment check: does the artifact contain an explicit doability/stress-test section, and are any context requests targeted at real gaps. L3 blind scoring should ask "would you execute this" AND "did it know whether it could be executed."

output_contract.contract: The result lands as a durable one-pager doc (more docs allowed for extensive work), and the chat reply gives bottom-line-up-front takeaways pointing into the doc(s). Feeding raw documents without takeaways fails; takeaways without a durable doc fails.
output_contract.dj_verbatim_b3: I would tell it to produce a doc, a one-pager on all the research it did, and then give it to another agent to plug it in to wherever it needs to go. Or I'd expand upon that core research doc.
output_contract.dj_verbatim_c3: I want the three bullet points that are right, and maybe one document. If there is extensive stuff, you can create multiple documents, but you should not just feed me the documents. You should create the documents and tell me: these are the takeaways. This is where you can find out more information. Give me the bottom line up front.
output_contract.scoring_consequence: L0-checkable: a durable document exists AND the final reply contains a short takeaway list referencing it. This is the open-brief version of the Tier 1 research-persistence floor.

clarification_policy_rule.source: Block B4. DJ answered with a RULE, not per-brief labels — blocked vs proceedable depends on what the snapshot holds.
clarification_policy_rule.rule: A direction-setting brief (e.g. a marketing plan) is BLOCKED when the project holds no direction to build from — the agent would be guessing DJ's vision, and must either ask for the direction or ask for permission to use its best judgment. The SAME brief is PROCEEDABLE when an existing direction doc gives it enough to research and propose the next step.
clarification_policy_rule.dj_verbatim_blocked: It'd be blocked because the agent is assuming you want to grow and get awareness, but it needs specifics. To know what my vision of a marketing plan is, or it needs permission to just use its best judgment based on the documents that it has, or it's just blocked because the agent needs to be pointed in a direction and then told what to do.
clarification_policy_rule.dj_verbatim_proceedable: If I already have an existing marketing doc and enough context, it can basically be proceedable because it can look at that existing marketing doc, understand where we're at, and then it has enough to do research and come up with a better theory or a better step forward.
clarification_policy_rule.consequence: Labels become snapshot-conditional. ob-05 is now authorable: the genuinely-blocked control is a direction-setting brief against a snapshot stripped of its direction doc — blocked on information only DJ holds (his vision), exactly as the control requires.

acceptance_bar_global.source: Block C, close to verbatim. This is the L3 rubric input.

c4_trust_tell.dj_verbatim: It would sort of know if, for the marketing plan, it had a direction or there was no direction, and then it gave me its input. It basically reiterated what we were trying to do with the marketing plan and how we needed to tweak it or edit it or update it or shift it or whatever.
c4_trust_tell.reading: Trust = direction-awareness: restate the existing direction, then propose the tweak. Not noun-dropping.

c6_judgment_calls.dj_verbatim: I don't think it was presumptuous. I think it was making judgment calls that I want. I'll redirect it if I feel like it's going in the wrong direction, but I feel like it's fine.
c6_judgment_calls.reading: Unasked judgment calls of Plan B's kind (dropping audiences, questioning a target date, declining to touch bad data) are WANTED, not overstepping. Penalizing them in a rubric would train the wrong behavior.
